did_you_know.text: Did you know? Proverbs presents integrity and walking uprightly as better than crooked or deceitful speech, even when a person is poor.
Did you know? This verse warns that good intentions are not enough: acting without knowledge and on impulse can lead to sin.
Did you know? According to this verse, a person may ruin his way through his own foolishness—and then turn his anger against the Lord instead of examining his responsibility for his actions.
Did you know? Proverbs portrays wealth as something that brings a person more friends, while poverty may cause friends to distance themselves.
Did you know? The chapter repeats the warning that a false witness will not go unpunished; lying is presented not merely as a moral flaw, but as an act with consequences.
Did you know? Acquiring wisdom and understanding is described here as loving one’s own soul: those who guard their understanding act for their own good and find what is good.
Did you know? Proverbs connects understanding with self-control: a person of insight is slow to anger, and overlooking an offense is considered his glory.
Did you know? A house and wealth may be inherited from one’s parents, but a wise wife is described in the chapter as a gift from the Lord.
Did you know? The chapter describes anyone who shows kindness to the poor as lending to the Lord; kindness toward the needy is presented as an act for which the Lord will repay him.
Did you know? A person may make many plans, but Proverbs emphasizes that it is the Lord’s purpose that will stand and be fulfilled.
